options.text: The geometry around 'N' atom in trimethylamine is pyramidal
The geometry around N atom in trisilylamine is planar

The nitrogen atom in trimethylamine is <math><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> -hybridized; whilst in trisilylamine it is <math><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> -hybridized
Trisilylamine has donor properties; whilst trimethylamine has no donor properties

solution.text:
In trimethylamine, 'N' atom is sp3 -hybridized.

Due to the presence of lone pair in sp3 -hybrid orbital, the geometry of (CH3)3N becomes pyramidal around nitrogen.

This lone pair of electrons can be donated to electron-deficient species, e.g., (CH3)3N→BF3 . This lone pair cannot be transferred to carbon atom, because carbon atom has no d-orbital in its valence shell.
In (SiH3)3N, the 'N' atom is sp2 -hybridized.

The orientation of three sp2 -hybrid orbitals is plane-triangular, therefore, the geometry around 'N' becomes plane-triangular. Here the lone pair of electrons is transferred to vacant d-orbitals to each of three silicon atoms forming pπ-dπ multiple bonds. Consequently, SiH33N has no donor properties. For example
(SiH3)3N+BF3→ No reaction.

                          NCl3 > NH3 > NF3

options.text: The geometry around 'N' atom in trimethylamine is pyramidal

Trisilylamine has donor properties; whilst trimethylamine has no donor properties

solution.text:
In trimethylamine, 'N' atom is sp3 -hybridized.

Due to the presence of lone pair in sp3 -hybrid orbital, the geometry of (CH3)3N becomes pyramidal around nitrogen.

This lone pair of electrons can be donated to electron-deficient species, e.g., (CH3)3N→BF3 . This lone pair cannot be transferred to carbon atom, because carbon atom has no d-orbital in its valence shell.
In (SiH3)3N, the 'N' atom is sp2 -hybridized.

The orientation of three sp2 -hybrid orbitals is plane-triangular, therefore, the geometry around 'N' becomes plane-triangular. Here the lone pair of electrons is transferred to vacant d-orbitals to each of three silicon atoms forming pπ-dπ multiple bonds. Consequently, SiH33N has no donor properties. For example
(SiH3)3N+BF3→ No reaction.
